richContent.text: Welcome to the guided tour of TXT → Learn. You will move through the eight slide kinds—intro, hero, teach, proof, comparison, quiz, summary, and CTA—with one continuous idea running underneath. The teach slide is our component museum: every block and media pattern stacked on purpose. The hero, proof, comparison, and summary stops reuse that same idea so you can see layout differences, not different stories.

showcase-hero.title: One calm arc for every lesson
showcase-hero.subtitle: Hook your reader first—the hero layout, not the teach canvas.

richContent.text: We keep returning to one claim: build lessons with credibility up front, truth in the middle, tension named honestly, and a clear response. Colossians 4:6 will be our anchor verse again on the proof slide. Here you only see the hook: headline, subtitle, and the hero screen layout (layout: hero) before we pile blocks on the teach slide.

showcase-main.title: The component museum (teach layout)
showcase-main.subtitle: Everything you can place on a stamped teach slide—composed in one pass so rhythm stays readable.

richContent.text: This opening band is deliberate: badge and trust strip establish credibility before anyone reads a paragraph. Stats give a quick scan of scope; icon features telegraph structure—so the eye knows where to land.

The proof grid previews the three body beats. Scripture below repeats Colossians 4:6—you will see it again on the proof-only slide with a different screen layout. Objection / answer names the worry in the room; the comparison block here is embedded in teach—the next comparison section uses the full comparison template.

Below FAQ you will see an inline CTA band, expandable depth, then audio. The media rail stacks image, video, before/after slider, and image grid—every media pattern beside the content column. After this museum we isolate proof, comparison, summary so each layout is visible.
